edges.description: Unrepaired DNA interstrand crosslinks cause genomic instability and p53-dependent depletion of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, culminating in bone marrow failure.
Defective DNA interstrand crosslink repair in Fanconi anemia predisposes patients to head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
edges.target: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

edges.description: Critically short telomeres cause premature replicative exhaustion of hematopoietic stem cells, leading to bone marrow failure.
Altered telomere maintenance and premature replicative cellular exhaustion in pulmonary tissues lead to pulmonary fibrosis.
Altered telomere maintenance and premature replicative cellular exhaustion in hepatic tissues lead to hepatic fibrosis and cirrhosis.
Impaired ribosomal subunit maturation triggers nucleolar stress and progenitor failure in the bone marrow.
Ribosome biogenesis defects in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cause exocrine pancreatic deficiency.
Ribosomal maturation defects in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome impair myeloid maturation, producing neutropenia alongside exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
Loss of MPL/THPO signaling impairs both megakaryopoiesis and multilineage hematopoietic stem cell maintenance, progressing to aplastic anemia.
Ineffective megakaryopoiesis causes severe congenital thrombocytopenia at birth.
Pro-inflammatory cytokines and TP53-dependent growth arrest and apoptosis deplete hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
Bone marrow failure precedes and selects for somatic escape or premalignant clones that evolve to myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.
Progressive multilineage hematopoietic stem cell depletion manifests clinically as peripheral blood pancytopenia.
Stress erythropoiesis in inherited marrow failure produces macrocytic anemia with elevated fetal hemoglobin.
Selection of somatic TP53- or RUNX1-mutated hematopoietic clones drives clinical progression to myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.

nodes.description: Oxymetholone and other androgens can temporarily improve blood counts, particularly in FA and TBDs. Androgens may upregulate telomerase activity.

evidence.reference_title: Bone marrow failure in telomere biology disorders: Current understanding and the emerging landscape of non-transplant therapies.
evidence.snippet: we review the clinical presentation, pathophysiology, surveillance, and non-HCT treatment of BMF in TBD, including supportive care, androgens, thrombopoietin receptor agonists, and investigational approaches

nodes.description: Common endpoint of all inherited aplastic anemias: progressive depletion of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells leading to hypocellular marrow and peripheral cytopenias. The rate of progression and specific lineage involvement vary by underlying genetic defect.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: The inherited marrow failure syndromes are a diverse set of genetic disorders characterized by hematopoietic aplasia and cancer predisposition. The clinical phenotypes are highly variable and much broader than previously recognized

evidence.reference_title: Bone marrow failure in telomere biology disorders: Current understanding and the emerging landscape of non-transplant therapies.
evidence.snippet: Bone marrow failure (BMF) is the most common hematologic complication of a TBD and can precede the development of more difficult-to-treat malignant transformation

nodes.description: Chronic replicative stress and genomic instability in the residual HSC compartment select for clones with acquired somatic mutations, commonly involving TP53, RUNX1, and RAS pathway genes. This drives progression to myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia.

evidence.reference_title: Predisposition to myeloid malignancies in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome: biological insights and clinical advances.
evidence.snippet: Genomic analysis revealed that most myeloid malignancies in patients with SDS have biallelic loss-of-function TP53 mutations. Single-cell DNA sequencing of SDS bone marrow samples can detect premalignant biallelic TP53-mutated clones before clinical diagnosis

evidence.reference_title: Inherited Predispositions to Myeloid Neoplasms: Pathogenesis and Clinical Implications.
evidence.snippet: germline predisposition to myeloid neoplasms is also associated with a wide range of other syndromes, including SAMD9/9L associated predisposition, GATA2 deficiency, RASopathies, ribosomopathies, telomere biology disorders, Fanconi anemia, severe congenital neutropenia, Down syndrome, and others

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: the cumulative incidences of these respective complications were around 50, 25, and 10%

nodes.description: First-line treatment for Diamond-Blackfan anemia. The 2024 international consensus recommends lowering the maintenance dose to a maximum of 0.3 mg/kg per day.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis, treatment, and surveillance of Diamond-Blackfan anaemia syndrome: international consensus statement.
evidence.snippet: These changes include lowering the prednisone maintenance dose to maximum 0·3 mg/kg per day, raising the pre-transfusion haemoglobin to 9-10 g/dL independent of age, recommending early aggressive chelation, broadening indications for haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation

nodes.description: The Fanconi anemia pathway repairs DNA interstrand crosslinks through coordinated monoubiquitination of FANCD2/FANCI and recruitment of downstream nucleases and homologous recombination machinery. Loss of any FA pathway component leads to unrepaired DNA damage, chromosomal instability, p53-mediated apoptosis of hematopoietic progenitors, and progressive marrow failure.

evidence.reference_title: The ubiquitination machinery of the Fanconi Anemia DNA repair pathway.
evidence.snippet: Central to the FA pathway is the monoubiquitination of FANCI-FANCD2 mediated by a ubiquitin RING-E3 ligase complex called the FA core complex. Genetic mutation in any component of the FA core complex results in defective FANCI-FANCD2 monoubiquitination and phenotypes of DNA damage sensitivity, birth defects, early-onset bone marrow failure and cancer

evidence.reference_title: Mechanism, specificity, and function of FANCD2-FANCI ubiquitination and deubiquitination.
evidence.snippet: Fanconi anemia (FA) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in any of the currently 22 known FA genes. The products of these genes, along with other FA-associated proteins, participate in a biochemical pathway, known as the FA pathway. This pathway is responsible for the repair of DNA interstrand cross-links (ICL) and the maintenance of genomic stability in response to replication stress

nodes.description: Cardinal feature of Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, with pancreatic lipomatosis replacing normal acinar tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Predisposition to myeloid malignancies in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome: biological insights and clinical advances.
evidence.snippet: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS) is an inherited multisystem ribosomopathy characterized by exocrine pancreatic deficiency, bone marrow failure, and predisposition to myeloid malignancies

nodes.description: FA patients have dramatically elevated risk of squamous cell carcinomas of the head and neck, with risk further increased after bone marrow transplantation.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: The most common malignancies were AML, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), liver tumors, vaginal SCC, and brain tumors

nodes.description: Only curative therapy for the bone marrow failure component. Reduced-intensity conditioning regimens have improved outcomes in FA and DC patients. In TBDs, toxicities of the conditioning regimen can be detrimental to other organs.

evidence.reference_title: Established and emerging non-cellular therapies in inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) remains the only curative modality in eligible IBMF patients but the indications are individualized due to significant transplant-related morbidity, including secondary cancer

evidence.reference_title: Bone marrow failure in telomere biology disorders: Current understanding and the emerging landscape of non-transplant therapies.
evidence.snippet: While allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) is curative for BMF in TBD, toxicities of the conditioning regimen can be detrimental to other organs. Balancing the risk of malignant transformation with HCT toxicity is a core challenge for providers who care for patients with TBD-associated BMF

nodes.description: Liver fibrosis and cirrhosis are recognized complications of telomere biology disorders, reflecting telomere attrition in hepatocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited Telomere Biology Disorders: Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, Diagnostics, and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: altered telomere maintenance as observed in TBDs typically results in premature replicative cellular exhaustion in the respective organ systems eventually leading to life-threatening complications such as bone marrow failure (BMF), pulmonary fibrosis, and liver cirrhosis

nodes.description: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia results from loss-of-function mutations in MPL (thrombopoietin receptor) or rarely THPO (thrombopoietin ligand). Absent thrombopoietin signaling causes ineffective megakaryopoiesis with severe thrombocytopenia at birth, progressing to pancytopenia and aplastic anemia during early childhood as HSC maintenance is also compromised.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia - Not a single disease.
evidence.snippet: CAMT in a narrow sense, which is primarily restricted to the hematopoietic system, is caused mainly by mutations in the gene for the thrombopoietin receptor (MPL), sometimes in the gene for its ligand (THPO)

nodes.description: Pro-inflammatory cytokines including TGF-beta, IL-1beta, and IFN-alpha mediate cytopenias across inherited bone marrow failure syndromes. Different germline stresses converge on TP53-dependent growth arrest and apoptosis of hematopoietic stem, progenitor, and precursor cells, with inflammatory cytokines playing a pathogenic role in both cytopenias and transformation to myeloid neoplasia.

evidence.reference_title: The Molecular and Genetic Mechanisms of Inherited Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes: The Role of Inflammatory Cytokines in Their Pathogenesis.
evidence.snippet: an overarching hypothesis states that different stresses elicit TP53-dependent growth arrest and apoptosis of hematopoietic stem, progenitor, and precursor cells. Here, we review the IBMFSs and propose a role for pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as TGF-β, IL-1β, and IFN-α, in mediating the cytopenias

nodes.description: Macrocytic anemia is characteristic, with elevated fetal hemoglobin and elevated erythrocyte adenosine deaminase activity.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Blood counts usually demonstrate macrocytic anemia with reticulocytopenia, often with and Hb F, as well as elevated red cell adenosine deaminase in more than 85% of patients.

nodes.description: Neutropenia is a hallmark of Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, often present from infancy and contributing to recurrent infections.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: several children with malabsorption due to pancreatic insufficiency also had neutropenia

nodes.description: Reduction in all three blood cell lineages (erythrocytes, leukocytes, platelets) due to progressive bone marrow failure. In FA, blood pancytopenia is the most common presentation with elevated MCV and fetal hemoglobin.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Blood pancytopenia was the most common presentation, particularly when the red cell mean cell volume (MCV) and fetal hemoglobin (Hb F) were elevated for age

nodes.description: All inherited bone marrow failure syndromes carry elevated risk of myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukemia. In FA, the relative risk for AML is more than 600-fold compared to the general population.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: the risk for AML was more than 600-fold, for HNSCC it was ~500-fold, and for vaginal SCC it was about 3000-fold

evidence.reference_title: Predisposition to myeloid malignancies in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome: biological insights and clinical advances.
evidence.snippet: Clinical outcomes for patients with SDS who develop myeloid malignancies are extremely poor because of high treatment-related toxicities and a high rate of refractory disease/relapse even after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT)

nodes.description: Pulmonary fibrosis is a major non-hematologic complication of telomere biology disorders, resulting from critically short telomeres in lung epithelial cells.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited Telomere Biology Disorders: Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, Diagnostics, and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: altered telomere maintenance as observed in TBDs typically results in premature replicative cellular exhaustion in the respective organ systems eventually leading to life-threatening complications such as bone marrow failure (BMF), pulmonary fibrosis, and liver cirrhosis

nodes.description: Diamond-Blackfan anemia and Shwachman-Diamond syndrome result from defects in ribosomal protein genes or ribosome assembly factors. Impaired ribosome biogenesis activates nucleolar stress, stabilizes p53, and triggers selective apoptosis of erythroid precursors (DBA) or neutrophil precursors (SDS).

evidence.reference_title: Predisposition to myeloid malignancies in Shwachman-Diamond syndrome: biological insights and clinical advances.
evidence.snippet: The pathobiology of SDS results from impaired ribosomal maturation due to the deficiency of SBDS and the inability to evict the antiassociation factor eIF6 from the 60S ribosomal subunit

nodes.description: Transfusion support with iron chelation therapy for transfusion-dependent patients. Growth factor support (G-CSF, EPO) in selected cases.

evidence.reference_title: Pathophysiology and management of inherited bone marrow failure syndromes.
evidence.snippet: Patients with severe or symptomatic neutropenia may benefit from granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF), particularly if they experience recurrent or life-threatening neutropenia-related infections.

nodes.description: Telomere biology disorders arise from defects in telomerase (TERT, TERC, DKC1), shelterin components (TINF2), or telomere replication helicases (RTEL1). Critically short telomeres trigger replicative senescence and apoptosis preferentially in highly proliferative tissues including hematopoietic stem cells. Telomere length below the first percentile for age is a diagnostic hallmark.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited Telomere Biology Disorders: Pathophysiology, Clinical Presentation, Diagnostics, and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: Premature aging due to critically short telomere length (TL) can also result from pathogenic germline variants in the telomerase complex or related genes that typically counteract replicative telomere shortening in germline and certain somatic cell populations, e.g., hematopoetic stem cells

evidence.reference_title: Bone marrow failure in telomere biology disorders: Current understanding and the emerging landscape of non-transplant therapies.
evidence.snippet: Telomere biology disorders (TBDs) are a heterogeneous group of inherited systemic diseases caused by pathogenic variants in genes encoding telomerase or proteins involved in telomere maintenance or protection. With very short and/or dysfunctional telomeres, patients with TBD have clinical manifestations clustered in tissues with high rates of cell proliferation

evidence.reference_title: Comparison of flow-FISH and MM-qPCR telomere length assessment techniques for the screening of telomeropathies.
evidence.snippet: Assessment of telomere length (TL) in peripheral blood leukocytes is part of the diagnostic algorithm applied to patients with acquired bone marrow failure syndromes (BMFSs) and dyskeratosis congenita (DKC)

nodes.description: Often the earliest hematologic manifestation, particularly in FA and CAMT.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia - Not a single disease.
evidence.snippet: Congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (CAMT) is a rare inherited bone marrow failure syndrome (IBMFS) that is characterized by severe thrombocytopenia at birth due to ineffective megakaryopoiesis and development towards aplastic anemia during the first years of life
